## 25. Why every fixed height moment becomes finite in large dimension

The partition construction has a dimension-independent growth exponent. But the differential forms constructed from it may still grow as a power of height when their arithmetic geometry becomes thin. The next theorem, SMom, must prove that this growth is integrable. The source establishes a concrete sufficient threshold: for a nonnegative integer moment order $A$, every matrix dimension $N\geq A+2$ admits a finite-volume arithmetic fundamental domain with finite integral of the height power of order $A$.

### Reducing an unbounded geometry to diagonal coordinates

The source first makes a rational change of basis in the adelic group, which describes the number field at its infinite and finite places together. The reduced basis is built by choosing a rational row of least adelic height and applying the same construction to the remaining block. The minimum exists because a bounded-height family of rational lines has finitely many representatives up to rational scaling. This follows using the product formula, discreteness of rational vectors, and compact representatives of idele classes in a bounded positive interval of modules.

A two-row approximation supplies the crucial inequality between adjacent diagonal entries. The source uses a pigeonhole argument in the coefficient box of an integral basis: more candidate integral multiples than small subboxes force two multiples to have close fractional coordinates. Their difference gives a nonzero rational row of controlled norm. Applied to the last two rows of a triangular matrix, the approximation bounds their diagonal ratio because the last row was chosen to have minimal height.

## 24. Constructing a smooth partition with controlled arithmetic growth

The preceding three analytic estimates now have to be applied to an actual differential form representing the cocycle that we started with. An arbitrary representative need not be square-integrable. The source addresses this by constructing a partition of unity whose derivatives grow at most as the first power of an arithmetic height. This growth control is a substantive part of the proof, not merely a technical choice of coordinates.

### A lattice can become thin in two different ways

At each infinite place, a positive definite Hermitian matrix specifies a quadratic metric on the embedded arithmetic lattice. Let $\lambda(h)$ denote its shortest nonzero squared lattice length. The source also considers the metric with blocks $(h_w^{-1})^T$, and writes its minimum as $\lambda_D(h)$.

The transpose is significant: the pairing in the arithmetic dual calculation is bilinear over the number field, rather than the usual real Euclidean pairing. The actual metric dual of the embedded integral lattice involves the trace pairing and the discriminant. Those factors must be retained when the source uses lattice transference.

The height is the reciprocal product of these two minima. Scaling all the original metric blocks by a common positive number multiplies the primal minimum by that number and divides the dual minimum by it. The product is unchanged.

For example, take a two-dimensional lattice metric with diagonal entries $t$ and $1/t$, with $t\geq 1$, over the Gaussian integers. Both squared minima are $1/t$, so the height is $t^2$. The determinant remains one throughout. Consequently the determinant alone would not detect this degeneration, whereas the height grows with it.

# CM5 R0: actual compact-cover scalar Ext comparison

## Scope

Parent candidate: PR #3807, exact corrected head
`3b191ec2d5d0f6e9ab62e53b9a9d6c57ff9c53ee`.
Let p:P→T be an epimorphism from a profinite space onto a compact
Hausdorff space. Write R_n for the genuine closed equal-image
(n+1)-tuple space, C_n for its actual free condensed module,
M=F(T), and D for the discrete integer coefficient object.
The parent constructs the exact augmented Cech complex and proves
all positive Ext(C_n,D) vanish. No projectivity of arbitrary
relation terms is assumed.

## Construction

The new Lean modules construct K_0=M and K_(n+1) as the actual
kernel at C_n. Exactness gives short exact sequences
0→K_(n+1)→C_n→K_n→0. The Yoneda extension class of each sequence
induces the connecting maps. Relative acyclicity of the middle
term proves that each connecting map is surjective; in positive
source degree it is bijective.

A degree-(n+1) Hom cocycle on C_(n+1) factors uniquely through
the epic map onto K_(n+1). The first connecting map sends this
factor to Ext^1(K_n,D), and iteration of the positive-degree
connecting isomorphisms gives Ext^(n+1)(M,D).
This map is additive and surjective. Exactness identifies its
kernel with the restrictions of morphisms C_n→D, precisely the
coboundaries. The scalar Hom equivalence is additive and intertwines
the actual alternating face differential, so the same map induces
an additive equivalence from the quotient of scalar cocycles by
scalar coboundaries to actual positive Ext.

The declarations are:

- CompactCoverExtTransfer: actual syzygy short exact sequences;
  conditional transfer of scalar exactness to all positive Ext.
- CompactCoverExtClasses: genuine Yoneda connecting maps, positive

# SCC-001: Target-relative gluing and compositional transport

Status: exploratory author-derived propositions, bounded exact finite replay, no formal certification or novelty claim. Continuation of [SCC-001](https://github.com/grandchallenge/MATHSOLVE/issues/1309) and [syzygy transport](SYZYGY_TRANSPORT.md). Public [illustrated chapter](https://grandchallenge.ai/MATH-PROGRAMME/scc/).

## 1. Mark a target, rather than a gate

Let B be the Boolean function algebra over F2, V contain constants and coordinates, and F_r be the predecessor filtration. Fix a single Boolean decision function f. Let B_0 and B_1 be the two support ideals determined by f=0 and f=1. Define N_r=F_r+fF_r, and the target-relative gluing space G_r=N_r/F_r. Equivalently, N_r is the direct sum of the two independent restrictions (embedded by zero extension) of F_r to the target's zero and one regions. This follows because (1+f)a=a+fa. Thus G_r measures the gap between independent realizability in the two regions and joint realizability by a single expression in F_r.

Writing d_r=dim G_r,

$$
d_r=\dim(fF_r)+\dim((1+f)F_r)-\dim F_r.
$$

It follows that d_r is nonnegative and at most the smaller of the two restriction dimensions, hence at most the smaller support-cell size. The marked class f+F_r is zero precisely when f belongs to F_r. Unlike the whole G_r, this marked class detects target completion at r=1.

## 2. A common algebra for successive gates

The Rees algebra R=sum over r>=0 of F_r z^r is a graded subalgebra of B[z]; z is formal and represents a one-step increase of allowed degree. Put N=R+fR and G=N/R. As a graded R-module,

$$
G\cong R/J_f,\qquad J_f=\{a\in R:fa\in R\}.
$$

/-- Exact integer version of the first-moment exponent comparison. -/
theorem firstMomentExponent (M n a k : Nat) (hk : 4 ≤ k)
    (hka : n * a = 6 * k) (hM : M ^ 12 ≤ 2 ^ a) :
    2 * M ^ n < 2 ^ k := by
  apply (Nat.pow_lt_pow_iff_left (n := 12) (by decide)).mp
  calc
    (2 * M ^ n) ^ 12 = 2 ^ 12 * (M ^ 12) ^ n := by
      rw [Nat.mul_pow, ← Nat.pow_mul, Nat.mul_comm n 12, Nat.pow_mul]
    _ ≤ 2 ^ 12 * (2 ^ a) ^ n := Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (Nat.pow_le_pow_left hM n)
    _ = 2 ^ (12 + 6 * k) := by
      rw [← Nat.pow_mul, Nat.mul_comm a n, hka, ← Nat.pow_add]
    _ < 2 ^ (k * 12) := Nat.pow_lt_pow_right (by decide) (by omega)
    _ = (2 ^ k) ^ 12 := Nat.pow_mul _ _ _

 theorem filter_or_le {α : Type} (xs : List α) (p q : α → Bool) :
    (xs.filter (fun x => p x || q x)).length ≤ (xs.filter p).length + (xs.filter q).length := by
  induction xs with
  | nil => simp
  | cons x xs ih =>
    cases hp : p x <;> cases hq : q x <;> simp [hp, hq] at * <;> omega
 theorem union_bound {α : Type} (xs : List α) (events : List (α → Bool)) (B : Nat)
    (h : ∀ p ∈ events, (xs.filter p).length ≤ B) :
    (xs.filter (fun x => events.any (fun p => p x))).length ≤ events.length * B := by
  induction events with
  | nil => simp
  | cons p ps ih =>
    have hp := h p (by simp)
    have hps := ih (fun q hq => h q (by simp [hq]))
    have hle := filter_or_le xs p (fun x => ps.any (fun q => q x))
    simp only [List.any_cons, List.length_cons, Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul]
    omega
 theorem exists_avoids {α : Type} (xs : List α) (events : List (α → Bool)) (B : Nat)
    (h : ∀ p ∈ events, (xs.filter p).length ≤ B)
    (hlt : events.length * B < xs.length) : ∃ x ∈ xs, ∀ p ∈ events, p x = false := by
  classical
  apply Classical.byContradiction
  intro hn
  have hall : ∀ x ∈ xs, events.any (fun p => p x) = true := by
    intro x hx
    cases he : events.any (fun p => p x) with
    | true => rfl
    | false =>
      exfalso
      apply hn
      refine ⟨x,hx,?_⟩
      intro p hp
      have hnot := List.any_eq_false.mp he p hp
      cases hpx : p x <;> simp_all
  have heq := List.filter_eq_self.mpr hall
  have hu := union_bound xs events B h
  rw [heq] at hu
  omega

def bits : Nat → List (List Bool)
  | 0 => [[]]
  | n+1 => (bits n).map (false :: ·) ++ (bits n).map (true :: ·)
def free : List (Option Bool) → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | none :: ms => free ms + 1
  | some _ :: ms => free ms
def fits : List (Option Bool) → List Bool → Bool
  | [], [] => true
  | none :: ms, _ :: bs => fits ms bs
  | some a :: ms, b :: bs => (a == b) && fits ms bs
  | _, _ => false
 theorem bits_length (m : Nat) : (bits m).length = 2^m := by
  induction m with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ m ih => simp [bits, ih, Nat.pow_succ, Nat.mul_two]
 theorem mask_count (ms : List (Option Bool)) :
    ((bits ms.length).filter (fits ms)).length = 2^(free ms) := by
  induction ms with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons a ms ih =>
    cases a with
    | none => simp [bits, free, fits, List.filter_map, Function.comp_def, ih, Nat.pow_succ, Nat.mul_two]
    | some b => cases b <;> simp [bits, free, fits, List.filter_map, Function.comp_def, ih]

/-- Finite first moment for a family of masks fixing exactly k of T coordinates. -/
theorem avoids_masks (T k : Nat) (ms : List (List (Option Bool)))
    (hk : k ≤ T) (hmask : ∀ m ∈ ms, m.length = T ∧ free m = T-k)
    (hc : ms.length < 2^k) :
    ∃ b ∈ bits T, ∀ m ∈ ms, fits m b = false := by
  have hbound : ∀ q ∈ ms.map fits, ((bits T).filter q).length ≤ 2^(T-k) := by
    intro q hq
    obtain ⟨m, hm, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hq
    obtain ⟨hmT, hfree⟩ := hmask m hm
    rw [← hmT, mask_count, hfree, hmT]
    exact Nat.le_refl _
  have hstrict : (ms.map fits).length * 2^(T-k) < (bits T).length := by
    rw [List.length_map, bits_length]
    calc
      ms.length * 2^(T-k) < 2^k * 2^(T-k) := Nat.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hc (Nat.pow_pos (by decide))
      _ = 2^T := by rw [← Nat.pow_add, Nat.add_sub_of_le hk]
  obtain ⟨b, hb, havoid⟩ := exists_avoids (bits T) (ms.map fits) (2^(T-k)) hbound hstrict
  refine ⟨b,hb,?_⟩
  intro m hm
  exact havoid (fits m) (List.mem_map.mpr ⟨m,hm,rfl⟩)
/-- Integer first-moment bound; the combinatorial encoding obligations remain explicit. -/
theorem first_moment_masks (M n a k T : Nat) (ms : List (List (Option Bool)))
    (hk : 4 ≤ k) (hkT : k ≤ T) (hka : n*a = 6*k) (hM : M^12 ≤ 2^a)
    (hcount : ms.length ≤ 2*M^n)
    (hmask : ∀ m ∈ ms, m.length = T ∧ free m = T-k) :
    ∃ b ∈ bits T, ∀ m ∈ ms, fits m b = false :=
  avoids_masks T k ms hkT hmask (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt hcount (firstMomentExponent M n a k hk hka hM))
